title: Tutorial: Name Instances With for_each
scenario: for_each creates one instance per key in a map or set. Unlike count, each instance keeps a stable address even when the collection changes. Create one bucket for every map entry.
constraints: Read the bucket name from each.value.
Export a map of bucket ids.

focus.title: Create named instances
focus.todo: Iterate over the map and use the current entry value as the bucket name.

hints.why: for_each protects stable addresses. Adding or removing a key changes only that key's instance, while a count list can shift every later index.
hints.what: Complete the bucket body with a per-key iteration and a reference to the current map value. The output already shows how to reshape the resulting instances into a map.
hints.when: Use for_each when each instance has a meaningful key, especially when instances may be added or removed over time.
hints.how: Read the output expression first: it iterates with name and bucket. The resource body has the same idea but only needs one iteration argument and one value reference. Avoid indexing a list here; the input is a map.

test_manifest.title: bucket_names is declared as a map
